notes: The very first kana. Think of it as 'ah' — like opening your mouth in surprise.
Sounds like 'ee' in 'eel'. Two short strokes standing side by side.
Sounds like 'oo' in 'food'. The little flick on top looks like a tail.
Sounds like 'e' in 'egg'. Looks a bit like an exotic bird strutting.
Sounds like 'o' in 'core'. Easy to confuse with あ — watch the extra loop.
Looks like a kite with its string trailing — 'ka' for kite.
Looks like a key — and it sounds like 'key' too.
A bird's open beak going 'coo'. One simple stroke.
Looks like a keg standing next to a stick. 'Ke' as in 'kettle'.
Two strokes lying flat, like a pair of coins stacked apart.
'Sa' as in 'salsa'. Mirror twin of ち — watch which way the hook faces.
One smooth stroke like a fishing hook. Pronounced 'shee', not 'si'.
A swirl in the middle — like soup ('su'-p) swirling in a bowl.
'Se' as in 'set'. A crossbar with two prongs poking up.
A zigzag like a sewing ('so'-ing) stitch.
Looks like a 't' and an 'a' squashed together — literally 'ta'.
Pronounced 'chee', not 'ti'. Mirror twin of さ.
Shaped like a tsunami wave. Pronounced 'tsoo' — the 'ts' of 'cats'.
'Te' as in 'ten'. A simple crossbar with a curving tail.
A toe with a splinter sticking out — 'to' for toe.
A cross up top with a small knot below. 'Na' as in 'nap'.
A needle ('ni'-dle) standing beside two short strokes.
Noodles with a loop at the end — slurp the 'nu'-dles.
A cat (neko) sitting with a curled tail — the loop is the tail.
A single loop, like a 'no entry' sign. You'll see it everywhere.
'Ha' as in laughter. Heads up: as the topic particle it's read 'wa'.
A wide smiling mouth saying 'hee hee'.
Between 'fu' and 'hu' — blow air softly like Mount Fuji's wind.
A little mountain. As the direction particle it's read 'e'.
Like は but with an extra roof on top — 'ho' for house.
Two crossbars and a loop, like a spool of thread. 'Ma' as in 'mama'.
Looks like the number 21 tangled together. 'Mi' as in 'me'.
A cow saying 'moo' — see the little face and the flick?
Like ぬ but without the loop. め also means 'eye'.
A fishhook with two worms — 'mo' bait catches 'mo' fish.
Looks like a yak's head with one horn. 'Ya' as in 'yacht'.
A fish swimming past a stick — a truly 'u'-nique ('yu'-nique) shape.
A yo-yo hanging from its string.
A hook with a small flag on top. Japanese 'r' is between 'r' and 'l'.
Two vertical strokes like a river ('ri'-ver) flowing down.
Like ろ but with a loop at the end — the loop is the 'ru' route.
Like ね but the tail flicks out instead of looping.
Like る without the loop — a road ('ro'-ad) with no roundabout.
Same family as ね and れ, but the tail curves in round — 'wa' for wide.
Pronounced just 'o'. Only used as the object particle — you'll see it constantly.
The only kana that's a lone consonant — a humming 'n' like in 'pen'.
